summary: Add a reversible host-local launch freeze for daemon replacement

replay.detail: No replicated claims or replay changes.

schema.detail: Adds the local_launch_freeze singleton table to local store initialization; freeze state is not replicated. Its schema and write sites, plus queued-operation owner adoption, are registered in the source-site large-value debt inventory; registration is not a value-size proof.

rules.detail: Launch workers and root-absent resource.lane.exec commands retain the same shared admission permit through physical spawn. Setting a freeze waits for earlier admitted workers before acknowledging. New launch operations remain durable and undispatched; finite program resource effects stay pending. Both retry after clear or expiry, retaining existing intent and incarnation fences. A restarted daemon adopts only never-dispatched queued operations; previously dispatched operations keep existing producer-recovery rules.

compatibility.detail: Adds GET/POST /v1/hosts/launch-freeze and POST /v1/hosts/launch-freeze/clear. Transport identity authenticates the owner using existing host-hold rules. Clear requires the same owner and activation id.

downtime.detail: Existing sessions, handoff delivery, subscriptions and mission runs continue; only new launches defer.

manual.detail: Use fractal hosts launch-freeze set --id ACTIVATION --reason REASON --duration-ms 900000 --wait-ms 5000 --as ACTOR before replacing the daemon. The spawn-drain wait defaults to 5 seconds and is capped at 10 seconds. Timeout or detached-producer uncertainty returns a typed refusal without arming a lease; abort activation before replacing anything. Read with fractal hosts launch-freeze show --json. Only after the new daemon reports ready, clear with fractal hosts launch-freeze clear --id ACTIVATION --as ACTOR. Maximum lease is 30 minutes; retrying the same active id does not extend it. The read includes queued operation ids and subjects.

recovery.detail: Freeze and queued operations survive daemon restart. Expiry makes the record inert and wakes deferred launch reconciliation. Failed activation must not clear early while replacement remains in progress; expiry bounds the interruption. Older binaries ignore this primitive, so rollback to an older daemon does not preserve the freeze guarantee.
